structured_output.summary:
P4 ground bedroom furnished in parts/room-29.mjs: lime bed (head east on the wall x58 z15), barrel nightstand with a standing lantern under the east window, and a hanging lantern from the ceiling; the lane (56,14)-(55,14)-(55,15) to the back door stays clear.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; my part places 3 blocks there because the shell is still a stub. A stand-in shell in /tmp/p36check gives 0 dark cells (min light 11), and the bed passes bed() with stand-in walls.
Not yet verified in the merged build: bed placement and the real walk check, both of which need the shell_b walls, floor and ceiling.
left: Real walk verdict unverified: `mcd room` on the stub build says no floor, and on the stand-in shell every cell reads unreachable because the outside isn't built. Re-run `mcd room build.nbt --rooms rooms.json --only "P4 ground bedroom"` after shell_b lands.
bed_set(56,3,15 east) was refused in the stub build (no wall at x58 z15, no floor); it is verified only against a stand-in shell. Confirm the bed placed after merge.
Barrel is the nightstand only, no chest (chest is not in palette.json); the room is 6 floor cells, so there's no seating or table. Furniture-wise it's a bed plus a bedside lamp.
No P4 ground bedroom checkbox exists in plan.md or elements.md, so nothing was ticked. The 'every room lit' item in elements.md is the global one.

waste.what: Checked the room by hand: I wrote a scratch script that reproduces the stub shell (walls, doorways, floor, ceiling) to run bed_set and the room check, because the real build has no shell yet.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls and a scratch directory in /tmp
waste.tool: a `mcd room --standin` (or a --shell-from-plan option) that fills a room's box with walls, floor, ceiling and doorway openings from rooms.json and plan.md, so a room can be tested before its neighbouring parts exist

waste.what: Worked out by hand the lane cells (the cells the 2-high walk from the partition door and the back door must keep clear) and the bed head/foot cells against the east wall.
waste.cost: a few minutes of coordinate reasoning on a 3x2 room
waste.tool: `mcd plan` could mark the lane (cells on the shortest walk from each doorway) and the cells a bed needs (head against a solid wall, 2 clear above), so the free cells are drawn, not derived
